problem: Existing visual navigation settings (PointNav, ImageNav, ObjectNav, VLN) ignore floor plans, a cheap and reliable prior, so agents need costly exploration. Prior floor-plan work relies on multi-sensor fusion (e.g. LiDAR) or constrains the floor-plan structure.
motivation: Humans navigate unfamiliar buildings using floor plans, which give global geometric and topological guidance. Using them with only RGB is hard for two reasons: the floor plan differs from the real layout (furniture is not drawn, which causes collisions), and RGB images and abstract sketches are different modalities, so localizing the agent on the plan is difficult.
key_idea: Use a diffusion policy conditioned on fused RGB and floor-plan features, goal position and an explicit (predicted or externally supplied) agent pose, so it learns collision-free navigation on a floor plan from demonstrations.
insight: Decoupling localization from planning works better than learning both end to end: Naive-FloNa is far below Loc-FloNa (GT), and better localization (retrained F3Loc at the agent's camera height) improves navigation. The diffusion policy tolerates imperfect input better than A*: Loc-FloNa (F3) beats Loc-A* (GT) in some settings at tau_c=inf, and it has fewer collisions than A* with the same localizer. Masking the floor-plan embedding (Loc-Diff) lowers SR/SPL, so the floor plan does contribute. Even so, noisy GT pose (0.1-0.5 m) drops SR from 68.4 to about 20-26.
method: Observation context: a shared EfficientNet-B0 (trained from scratch) encodes the last l RGB frames, another EfficientNet-B0 encodes the floor plan, and 4-layer/4-head multi-head attention fuses them into a 256-d context vector c_t.
Goal position: the marked floor-plan pixel is converted to world coordinates by p_g = u_g/mu + delta, using the floor-plan resolution and offset from F3Loc.
Naive-FloNa: a fully connected head f_p predicts the pose from c_t, trained end to end. An auxiliary head f_d predicts shortest-path distance to the goal, as in ViNT.
Loc-FloNa: the pose comes from outside, either GT or the pre-trained F3Loc localizer, and f_p is removed.

Diffusion policy: a conditional 1D U-Net (15 conv layers, K=10 denoising steps, square-cosine schedule) denoises a 2D displacement sequence conditioned on [c_t, p_g, pose]. Horizon H_p=32, executes the first H_a=16 steps.

Training: MSE noise loss plus lambda-weighted distance and pose losses (lambda1=lambda3=0.001, lambda2=0.005). Random future goals are sampled along trajectories. 5 epochs, AdamW lr 1e-4, batch 256, one RTX3090.
Collision recovery at test time: after a collision the agent rotates 45° clockwise and re-predicts actions.

setting.backbone: EfficientNet-B0 x2 + multi-head attention + conditional U-Net diffusion policy (trained from scratch); F3Loc localizer for the F3 variants
setting.training_data: Own FloNa dataset: 67 Gibson scenes, 11,575 A*-generated episodes (~26 h) with rendered RGB in iGibson; F3Loc retrained variant uses ~40k image-pose pairs at 80 cm height
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (512x512, 45° FoV) history + floor plan image + goal position on floor plan; pose from GT or F3Loc for Loc variants
setting.action_space: continuous 2D displacement a_t = p_t - p_{t-1} (action sequence of 16 executed steps)
setting.privileged: Loc-FloNa (GT) uses ground-truth agent pose at test time; the real-robot run uses LiDAR odometry from a manually annotated start pose in a pre-scanned scene. Naive-FloNa and Loc-FloNa (F3) use no GT pose.

numbers.eval_set_note: 50 test scenes, 10 start-goal pairs each (500 episodes)
numbers.backbone: EfficientNet-B0 + attention + diffusion U-Net, GT pose

numbers_note: Custom benchmark (FloNa) with no canonical name. Table 1 gives SR/SPL for tau_c in {10,30,50,inf} and tau_d in {0.25,0.30,0.35}; only some settings are listed here. Ablation Loc-Diff (GT, no floor plan) reaches SR 51.1 / SPL 49.8 at tau_c=inf, tau_d=0.30 (Table A2).
results: Loc-FloNa (GT) is best in every setting, e.g. SR 75.8 / SPL 55.2 at tau_c=inf, tau_d=0.3 m, versus 29.6 / 29.4 for Loc-A* (GT), the strongest baseline. With predicted localization (F3Loc), all methods drop sharply: Loc-FloNa (F3) reaches SR 30.8 and Naive-FloNa 24.8. Loc-FloNa also has fewer collisions than A* with the same localizer. A real-robot AGV deployment worked without fine-tuning, but only qualitatively.
limitations: Performance depends heavily on localization quality: with predicted F3Loc poses SR falls to about 30, and noisy GT poses drop SR to about 20-26.

Only clean architectural floor plans are supported (no hand-drawn sketches), and evaluation is on a single simulated dataset with a custom benchmark. Real-world results are qualitative only, with GT-like LiDAR odometry and a pre-scanned scene.
Collision avoidance is still imperfect: success rates fall sharply under tight collision budgets, e.g. tau_c=10.
